chunks: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Amr al-Attar in Balkh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mamduh narrated to us, saying: Humran narrated from Malik ibn Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Hasin, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said:

I was riding behind the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he said: 'O Mu'adh, do you know what is the right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon the servants?' - he repeated it three times - I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'The right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon the servants is that they do not associate anything with Him.' Then he said (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do you know what is the right of the servants upon Allah, the Mighty and High, if they do that?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'That He does not chastise them,' or he said: 'That He does not make them enter the Fire.'

key_terms.أَنْ لَا يُدْخِلَهُمْ النَّارَ: That He does not make them enter the Fire
key_terms.أَنْ لَا يُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا: That they do not associate anything with Him
key_terms.أَنْ لَا يُعَذِّبَهُمْ: That He does not chastise them

ai.seo_question: What is the right of Allah upon His servants and the right of the servants upon Allah according to Mu'adh ibn Jabal?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Tawhid*, this hadith establishes the reciprocal covenant between the Divine and the servant, where the primary obligation is *Tawhid* (monotheism) and the corresponding divine promise is deliverance from Hellfire. This narration underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the balance between human duty and divine mercy, linking correct belief directly to eschatological salvation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 28. Abu `Ali al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn `Amr al-`Attar said in Balkh, that Muhammad ibn Mahud said: Humran on the authority of Malik ibn Ibrahim ibn Tihman on the authority of [Abu] Hasin on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabl who said:

I was with the Messenger of Allah (sw) and he said to me, “O Mu`adh! Do you know what is the right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon His Servants?”, repeating it three times. I answered,” Allah and His Messenger know best.” The Messenger of Allah said: “The right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon His Servants is that they should not associate anything with Him.” After that he asked, “Do you know what the right of the servants is upon Allah, the Mighty and High, when they respect His Right?” I answered, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He (sw) said: “That He should not chastise them.” Or he (sw) said: “That He should not place them in Hell.”
